name: What types of trim are typically installed in a kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: What types of trim are typically installed in a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kitchen trim installation covers several finished carpentry elements that seal gaps and frame cabinetry. Common types include crown molding along the top of upper cabinets, baseboard molding where lower cabinets or walls meet the floor, light rail trim along cabinet bottoms to conceal under-cabinet lighting, and scribe molding. Scribe molding is thin, flexible trim cut specifically to mask uneven gaps between cabinet boxes and bowed walls. You may also need toe-kicks, filler strips between cabinets, and casing around kitchen windows or doorways to achieve a cohesive, finished appearance throughout the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen trim includes crown molding, baseboards, light rail trim, toe-kicks, and scribe molding used to cover gaps between cabinets, walls, and flooring.
